title: The document repository
summary: Browse, search and open every file filed against your customers, vehicles, quotes and job cards.

body.text: The **Documents** page is the central repository for every file in the CRM — uploads, generated PDFs, proofs of payment, delivery photos and more. You only ever see files you are permitted to access, and download and management actions are re-checked on the server.
What each row shows

items: The file name, type icon and size
Where it is filed: Customer, Vehicle, Quote or Job card (or "Unfiled")
Any tag (for example invoice, pop, delivery-note)
Who uploaded it and when
An "old version" marker on superseded files

body.text: Finding a file

items: Type part of the file name into the search box and choose Search.
Open or preview a file by clicking its name, or use the external-link icon to open it in a new tab.
Use the Version history toggle to include superseded files; switch back to Current versions to hide them again.

body.text: The list shows up to 250 of the most recent accessible files. Narrow the view with search rather than scrolling.
If you manage templates, the Templates & Studio button in the header takes you to Document Studio.

title: Uploading and organising documents
summary: Upload files, rename and tag them, re-file them against a record, and replace them with a new version.

body.text: Uploading needs the documents.upload permission; renaming, moving and replacing need documents.manage. If you do not have these, the upload box and Manage button will not appear.
Upload a file

items: In the upload box on the Documents page, choose a file.
Select Upload. The file is filed into the repository and recorded in the audit log.

body.text: Files must be 25 MB or smaller. Larger files are rejected.
Rename or tag a file

items: Select Manage on the file's row.
Edit the name and pick a tag from the list (invoice, pop, delivery-note, delivery-photo, delivery-signature, checkin or other).
Choose Save.

body.text: Re-file a document against another record

items: Open Manage and go to "Move to a different record".
Pick a destination Customer, Vehicle or Quote.
Choose Move. You need access to the destination record for this to succeed.

body.text: Replace with a new version

items: Open Manage and use the "Upload a new version" section.
Choose the replacement file and select Replace.

body.text: Replacing keeps the previous file in history and marks it as an old version — nothing is lost. Use the Version history toggle to see superseded files.
Removing a document moves it to the Trash, where it is recoverable for 60 days before permanent deletion.

title: Document Studio overview
summary: Where managers control print layouts and build free-form documents, templates, clauses and merge fields.

body.text: **Document Studio** is the template workshop for the CRM. It is split into two clearly separated areas so every edit has a predictable production effect. Access requires the document_templates.manage permission.
The two areas

items: **Operational templates** — named layouts that control the CRM's existing print and PDF outputs (quotes, job cards and other document types), grouped by kind.
**Free-form Studio** — a standalone editor for building custom documents from blocks, reusable clauses and merge fields, for anything without a dedicated CRM screen.

body.text: The page also lists your **reusable clauses** and the most **recent free-form documents** that have been generated.

Quote signing additionally uses an editable Document Builder layout, reached via "Edit signing layout" on the Quote template card. Other document types stay on their existing renderers until each builder layout reaches visual parity.
Use the "Open document repository" button to jump straight to the Documents list.

title: Managing operational print templates
summary: Create and edit the named templates that drive the CRM's quote, job-card and document print layouts.

body.text: Operational templates feed the matching CRM print/PDF route. Each document type ships with a built-in template; you can add your own variants and choose which one is the default.
Create a template

items: Find the document type's card in the operational section.
Type a name for the new template.
Leave "Start from standard" selected, or pick an existing template to copy it.
Choose Create — the template opens for editing.

body.text: Edit template content

A template editor lets you set the **logo**, an **intro**, **body text**, **terms**, up to four **footer lines**, toggle each **section** on or off, and configure the **signature** block (position and whether the dealer counter-signs).

items: Set a template as the **Default** so it is used automatically for that document type.
**Duplicate** a template to branch a new variant.
**Replace the logo** by uploading an image (2 MB max).

body.text: You cannot delete the default template — set another template as default first. Every create, edit, default change and deletion is written to the audit log.
On the Quote card, "Edit signing layout" opens the editable Document Builder used when quotes are sent for signature.

title: Building free-form documents
summary: Compose custom proposals and letters from blocks, reusable clauses and merge fields, then finalise to a filed PDF.

body.text: The free-form Studio creates standalone documents — custom proposals, letters and handover packs — from blocks, clauses and merge fields. Managing templates and clauses needs document_templates.manage; creating a document needs documents.manage.
Templates, clauses and documents

items: **Free-form templates** are reusable starting points. Publish a template to create a numbered version; new documents draw from the latest published version (or the draft if none is published).
**Reusable clauses** are standard passages. They work only inside the free-form Studio and are copied in by value when inserted — later edits to the clause do not change documents already using it.
**Documents** are individual instances, optionally linked to a contact, lead or quote so merge fields fill automatically.

body.text: Create and finalise a document

items: Create a free-form template and edit its content, then Publish it.
Create a document from the template, linking a contact, lead or quote to populate merge fields.
Edit the draft as needed.
Finalise the document — the CRM renders it to a PDF and files it in the document repository.

body.text: Once a document is finalised it is locked. To change it, duplicate it and edit the copy. Deleting a document moves it to Trash.

title: Generating and signing builder documents
summary: Turn a Document Builder template bound to a quote or job card into a filed PDF, or prepare it for e-signing.

body.text: Document Builder templates can be generated against a live record and filed as a PDF, or prepared as a signature request. These actions are restricted to owner-level administrators.
Record binding rules

A document may be bound to at most one record — either a quote or a job card, never both. Each template also requires a compatible record type; binding the wrong type is rejected with a clear message.
Generate to the repository

items: Choose a compatible quote or job card for the template.
Generate the document — a PDF is produced, filed in the repository with a generated-pdf tag, and opened for you.
The action is recorded in the audit log.

body.text: Prepare for signing

items: Make sure the document has at least one recipient and signature field.
Send the document for signing — the CRM generates the PDF, files it, and creates a signature request.
Open the Signatures hub to send the request to recipients.

body.text: An empty document, or one with no recipients, cannot be sent — add a recipient and signature field first.

title: The document library
summary: Shared, versioned brochures, price lists and spec sheets so the team always sends the latest approved file.

body.text: The **Document library** holds shared reference material — brochures, price lists, spec sheets and warranty documents — with every file versioned so staff never send an outdated copy. Anyone signed in can browse and download; adding and removing files needs the library.manage permission.
Browse and download

items: Documents are grouped by category (Brochure, Price list, Spec sheet, Warranty, Other). Use the category chips to filter.
Each card shows the latest version, its size and who last updated it.
Choose "Download latest" to get the current approved file.
Expand "Version history" to download an earlier version.

body.text: Add documents

items: Select "Add documents".
Choose one or more files — each file becomes its own library document.
Pick a category that applies to all of them.
Optionally set a custom name (single file only), then Add to library.

body.text: Upload a new version

items: On a document card, choose "New version".
Select the replacement file and note what changed (for example "Updated 2026 pricing").
Upload — it becomes the new latest version and the old one stays in history.

body.text: The change note appears in the version history, so keep it specific. It helps the team see why a file was updated.
Removing a library document moves it and all its versions to the Trash for 60 days before permanent deletion.

title: Reading the reports dashboard
summary: Track leads, won deals, revenue, pipeline, sources, team performance and workshop output across any date range.

body.text: The **Reports** dashboard summarises sales and workshop performance. What you see is scoped to the records you are permitted to view: with reports.view_all you see everything, otherwise the figures are restricted to you and your team.
Choosing the period

items: Pick a range: month to date, last 30 days, quarter to date, year to date, last 12 months, or a custom from/to.
Every headline figure is compared against the equivalent previous period, shown as an up or down percentage.

body.text: Headline figures

rows: Leads marked won in the period
Total value of deals won, in rand
Won as a share of all closed (won plus lost) deals

body.text: Charts

items: **Sales trend** — new leads as a line and won-deal value as bars, with the previous period as a dashed line.
**Pipeline right now** — open leads by stage. This is a live snapshot and ignores the date range.
**Lead sources** — share of leads per channel with each channel's win rate.
**Team performance** — value of accessible deals won per team member.
**Workshop** — accessible job cards completed per period.

body.text: Filters

items: Use the filter bar to narrow by team member, product or lead source.
The pipeline snapshot respects the filters but not the date range.

body.text: You can only filter by team members whose records you are permitted to see.

title: Using the audit log
summary: Search the append-only history of who did what, with before/after changes and full request context.

body.text: The **Audit events** page is a tamper-resistant, append-only record of activity across the CRM. Viewing needs the audit.view permission; exporting needs audit.export.
What each event records

items: When it happened and who did it (actor name and type)
The event type and the affected entity, often as a direct link to the record
The changed fields, with full before and after values
Request context: source, IP address, correlation ID and user agent

body.text: Filtering the log

items: Narrow by event type, entity type or actor using the dropdowns.
Set a From and To date.
Search summaries or entity IDs with the search box.
Choose Filter, or Clear to reset.

body.text: The view shows up to the 500 newest matching events. Use the filters to reach older or more specific activity.
Exporting

items: Apply the filters you want in the export.
Choose "Export filtered CSV" — the current filters are carried through to the download.

body.text: Audit rows cannot be edited or deleted — the database blocks updates and deletes with triggers. The log is a permanent governance record.

title: Trash and restoring deleted items
summary: Deleted records are held for 60 days in the Trash, showing who removed them and why, and can be restored.

body.text: Deletions across the CRM are soft — records move to the **Trash** rather than disappearing. Anyone signed in can view the Trash; restoring an item is restricted to owner-level administrators.
What lands in the Trash
Deleted contacts, leads, vehicles, job cards, documents, products, library documents and quotes all appear here during their recovery window.
What each row shows

items: The item and its type
Who deleted it and the reason recorded at deletion
When it was deleted
How many days remain before permanent removal — shown in red when 7 days or fewer remain

body.text: Restore an item

items: Find the item in the Trash list (or the mobile cards).
Choose Restore — it returns to its normal location and the restore is recorded in the audit log.

body.text: Items are kept for **60 days**, then permanently deleted along with any stored files. Restore anything you need before its countdown reaches zero — permanent removal cannot be undone.
If Restore is not available to you, ask an administrator — restoring requires owner-level access.
